notes: STS-81 MECO targets: VI 25,915 ft/s (predicted; 25,922 flown, Missions Summary 2-98), the tape's flight-path angle 0.5 deg (STS-81's value NOT found), and the radius that makes the coast's apogee 159.9 nmi, the post OMS-2 apogee (OMS-2 at apogee raises the perigee): 53.19 nmi above PASS's equatorial radius.  104% throttle as STS-134 (K_CMD 104).  The rest as sts134-reconfig.json.

cells.name: CGGS_ASSUMED_SSME_FAIL_MET
cells.value: 0: no second-stage trajectory lofting (TFAIL, FSSR STS 83-0002-34 4.8: 'If trajectory lofting is desired (TFAIL is not zero)...'). No STS-134 value is published; with the tape's 218 s (lofting on until the RTLS/AOA boundary, also 218) PEG lofted second stage ~30,000 ft above the ASCENT ADI - NOMINAL card and dove at the boundary; with 0 its Hdot follows the card (flight p5) and the reserve at MECO is about STS-134's.

cells.name: CGGS_ROLL_CMD_CHANGE_V
cells.value: V_RHO_PHI (FSSR STS 83-0002-34 4.8; a second-stage I-load, not in the DOLILU or the 4.12 uplink groups): the Earth-relative velocity at which second-stage guidance commands PHI_2STG, the roll to heads-up.  The STS-134 Ascent Checklist's cue is 'VI = 13.2K Roll Heads Up'; on the simulated trajectory Vi - Vrel is about 1,207 ft/s there (flight p10: the tape's 12,500 started the roll at Vi ~13,700), so 12,000.

cells.name: GSE_SEP_CMD_DELAY
cells.value: V97U9753C SRB SEP command time delay, nominal: 4.42 s (release 6). GSESRB declares these as locals with the generic release's INITIAL values; the flight's I-loads replace them. With the release's 6 s command delay PASS separated ~6.1 s after the later SRM reached 50 psia, where STS-118 to STS-135 (nine mission reports, Appendix A) separated 4.32-4.80 s after it, mean 4.51 = 4.42 plus half of GSESRB's 0.16 s cycle (the code's -0.48 cancels its four-pass confirmation). Source: Booster Console Handbook (JSC-17239 Rev G, SCP 2.2.1, Table 2.2.1-I, SRB SEPARATION I LOAD SUMMARY), typical value.
